chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Nasr ibn Muzahim, from Ibn Lahi'a, from Abu Zar'a, from Abdullah ibn Razeen, from Ammar ibn Yasir (may Allah be pleased with him), that he said:

The call of the Ahl al-Bayt of your Prophet will come in the end of time, so hold fast to the earth and remain quiet until you see its leader. When the Turks confront the Romans and battles increase upon the earth, a caller will cry out from the walls of Damascus: 'Woe to the one who is near from the approaching evil!' and the wall of its mosque will be destroyed.

key_terms.آخِرِ الزَّمَانِ: The end of time / eschatological period
key_terms.دَعْوَةُ: The call or proclamation (of the Imam)
key_terms.قَادَتَهَا: Its leader (referring to the leader of the call)

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the end times regarding the Turks, Romans, and Damascus mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the 'Silsilat al-Dhahab' (Golden Chain) of transmission, underscoring the reliability of the report regarding the pre-reappearance signs. It emphasizes a period of strategic patience for the followers of the Ahl al-Bayt amidst escalating geopolitical turmoil, specifically the conflict between the Turks and Romans, which serves as a precursor to the Mahdi's emergence. The specific omen in Damascus, including the destruction of the mosque's wall, is interpreted by Shia scholars as a distinct marker of the end times, linking historical events to eschatological prophecy.
